newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hitachi plans 97/98 group chip output of Y880 bln.
newsitem.headline: Hitachi plans 97/98 group chip output of Y880 bln.

text.p: Japanese electronics maker Hitachi Ltd said on Thursday it plans 880 billion yen worth of group chip output in the current financial year which started in April, up 11 percent from the year before.
Hitachi said in a statement that it plans group capital spending in the semiconductor sector in 1997/98 of 150 billion yen, unchanged from the previous year.
Hitachi also expects group output of 16 megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips to slip to 10 million units per month by December from 11 million in May.
Output of next-generation 64 megabit DRAMs, meanwhile, is expected to rise to two million units per month by December and to three million by March 1998, from the current 300,000 units, it said.
Hitachi also said it forecast a 33 percent increase in group output of liquid crystal displays (LCDs) to 120 billion yen in 1997/98, after 50 percent growth in the previous year.
It said that, of that amount, group output of lower-cost super-twisted nematic (STN) LCDs is expected to grow 26 percent to 48 billion yen.
Hitachi's group capital spending in LCDs is expected to rise by 14 percent to 25 billion yen in 1997/98 from the previous year's 22 billion yen.
